section_1.title: The Concept of Pulse: Beats as Units of Time
section_1.content: Establish the foundation of music as a time-based structure. Introduce the 'Beat' as the fundamental unit of measurement, similar to the ticking of a clock.
section_1.example: A woodpecker drumming on a tree: each peck is a pulse. Visually represent this as a series of equidistant dots on a timeline.

section_2.title: Introduction to Measure (Bars)
section_2.content: Explain that music is organized into 'Measures' (or bars) to make it readable. Introduce the Time Signature as a mathematical fraction: Top number (beats per measure) over bottom number (the note type getting one beat).
section_2.example: A '4/4' time signature visualized as a box containing 4 quarter-note symbols. Think of it like a container that can only hold exactly 4 beats.

section_3.title: The Math of Note Values (Fractions)
section_3.content: Explain how different musical notes correspond to mathematical fractions. A whole note (1), half note (1/2), and quarter note (1/4). Prerequisite: Basic fraction addition.
section_3.example: A 'Pizza Partition' graphic: A whole circle (Whole note) divided into 4 slices (4 Quarter notes). Show that 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1 Measure.

section_4.title: Application: Composing with Constraints
section_4.content: Combine the time signature and note values to 'fill' a measure. This demonstrates how musicians use arithmetic to ensure the music flows correctly within its structural boundaries.
section_4.example: A robot musician trying to fill a 4/4 measure. If the robot plays two half-notes, the measure is full. If it plays one half-note and two quarter-notes, the measure is also perfectly full (2/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1).

section_5.title: Summary & The Universal Language
section_5.content: Recap that music is essentially applied math in time. Reiterate that measures allow us to organize patterns, making music predictable and beautiful.
section_5.example: A final animation showing a scrolling musical staff syncing perfectly with a mathematical number line, proving that rhythm is just counting in disguise.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We organize beats into measures.", "Time signatures define these boxes.", "Four beats fit in one measure."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction to Measure (Bars)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        bar_line1 = Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).set_length(3)
        bar_line2 = Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).set_length(3)
        beats = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00FF7F", fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        measure_box = VGroup(bar_line1, bar_line2, beats).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Position elements
        self.place_in_area(measure_box, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(bar_line1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        for beat in beats:
            self.play(FadeIn(beat, scale=0.5), run_time=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(bar_line2))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We organize beats into measures.", "Time signatures define these boxes.", "Four beats fit in one measure."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction to Measure (Bars)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        bar_line1 = Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).set_length(3)
        bar_line2 = Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).set_length(3)
        beats = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00FF7F", fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        measure_box = VGroup(bar_line1, bar_line2, beats).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Position elements
        self.place_in_area(measure_box, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(bar_line1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        for beat in beats:

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(Create(bar_line2))
        self.wait(1)
